html:
Nyasaland was the British protectorate that became Malawi, declared in 1891 as the British Central Africa Protectorate and renamed in 1907, with its capital at Zomba.

Settlers took much of the fertile Shire Highlands for coffee, cotton and tobacco estates, where Africans worked under a labour-tenancy system. Many men left to work in Southern Rhodesia and South Africa.

Grievances led to the Chilembwe rising of 1915. In 1953 the territory was forced into the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland, and protests against it, led by Hastings Banda from 1958, brought a state of emergency in 1959 and then independence as Malawi on 6 July 1964.
sum: Nyasaland was the British protectorate that became Malawi, declared in 1891 as the British Central Africa Protectorate and renamed in 1907, with its capital at Zomba.
